utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, could you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you and good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-03-67-T, the Prosecutor versus Vojislav Seselj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. This is Tuesday, and I welcome the Prosecution, our witness, and Mr. Seselj, as well as everyone in and around the courtroom helping us. Before moving on to the examination-in-chief, I would like to tell everyone that the Judges consulted each other regarding tomorrow's hearing. I told you at first that we would sit in the morning, but very unfortunately the Prlic case is sitting in the morning on a Rule 98 bis ruling at 9.00, and therefore the hearing cannot start as planned in the morning, but we could sit as of 12.00, and that way we could end up a bit earlier than expected. So the hearing will continue tomorrow, and we will start at 12.00. So we'll sit from 12.00 to 1.30. We'll have a short break, a short lunch break, and we'll resume at 2.00 or maybe 2.30 p.m. And we will sit until about 5.00 or 5.30. I wanted to say this. Secondly now. On Thursday we will have a hearing in the morning as planned. So this is the programme that we have devised. I will now give the floor to Prosecution. However, Mr. Seselj, you want the floor?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just have two short observations, Mr. President, and I think it's better that I warn you in time to avoid any problems with the beginning of the testimony. I'm talking about VS-034, that witness, now, the Prosecution has not provided me with a statement of the 8th of March 2005 of that witness in the Serbian language. I have it in English but English means nothing to me. They also provided me with previous three statements by that witness in Serbian, so the 8th of March, 2005 statement is what I need in the Serbian language urgently, and pursuant to the rules, I should have had that at least one month before the -- that witness comes in to testify, but I won't mind and won't be angry if you give it to me tomorrow or the day after and secondly I'd like to draw your attention to the following: Yesterday I received a supplement to the report of the expert witness Reynaud Theunens, and on one page, however, it does say that this was omitted by mistake earlier but it's very important. I mean if you take a look at that you'll see just how important it is for my defence. Now, I consider that this kind of practice on the part of the OTP should be stopped. I received this yesterday, just yesterday, and the witness started his testimony last week in this Trial Chamber within the frameworks of the examination-in-chief. So I think that that is absolutely impermissible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, I'd like to tell Prosecution that there are two items that are raised by Mr. Seselj, that one is very simple. Obviously the translation of the statement of the March 8, 2005 is missing in B/C/S. So I'm sure you'll be able to give him this document very quickly, maybe in the minutes to come.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we'll look into the disclosure issue of the statement, and I'll get back to you on this as soon as I have an answer, but I'm sure that this is something that we can take care of during the day. As for the issue of the report, it is correct that over the weekend I realised that there was a paragraph missing from the B/C/S translation of the report. So on yesterday morning we had the relevant part translated and provided to the accused. What is missing was the conclusion by the expert. This conclusion, though, as far as I can see, is also part of the summary part of the statement. So it's not as if there's something completely new that is being brought to the accused's attention. It is obviously regrettable that these sort of things happen, but I don't think there's any prejudice to the accused on this issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The conclusion that is at what page in the English version, please, could you tell us?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. It -- the conclusion is regarding the command and control structure of the SRS/SCP, and it is on page -- for some reason I only remember the B/C/S version right now. It's the page 151. Page 53 in part 2. The paragraph reads: "The existence of these reports," and here it talks about certain reports back and forth to the war staff, "The existence of these reports and their degree of details suggests that the SRS War Staff, in addition to" --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speaker kindly slow down, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, you're being asked by the interpreters to slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I'll start that paragraph over again in a proper speed. Sorry. "The existence of these reports and their degree of detail suggests that the SRS War Staff in addition to a command relationship also maintains a reporting relationship with the SRS/SCP volunteers participating in the conflict."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So as Mr. Seselj says, this is an important item, this conclusion drawn on page 53 of the English version should have been translated into B/C/S. Obviously there's been a glitch in the B/C/S -- in the translation department. And you discovered that this weekend, is that it?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. As I said, the contents of this paragraph is included in the summary session of the report. So I don't think the accused has been -- has not been informed about this particular conclusion of the expert, but of course the conclusion should also have been in this part of the report. That's obvious.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Seselj, you've heard what the Prosecutor just said. He discovered this fact himself. He discovered that this paragraph had been skipped in the B/C/S translation, and as soon as he found that out, of course, he told you about it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the Prosecutor says that this provision is to be found in the summary as well. Possibly it is there. I'm not going to look through the summary now, but the summary has general conclusions by the author of the report. So it is possible that that conclusion is contained therein. But I must be provided with the full and complete report. It would be the same thing if the Prosecutor were to say to me I could have read that conclusion somewhere else, in some earlier testimony by this witness, somewhere in the press, perhaps, or in a registrar bulletin or whatever, but I need to have the complete report, not to have to think about it myself, to see whether something in the -- is in the resume but not in the text of the report, whereas now it appears that it is contained in the text of the report. Secondly, Mr. President, in this report we have -- or, rather, the report was supplemented twice, two supplements. One part was secret and confidential and I was told that I could only receive it one month prior to trial and then there were two supplements, and then prior to the testimony itself there were two corrections made to the report and a large number of corrections in two acts -- two documents that I was supplied with, which testifies to the lack of seriousness in which this report was prepared and this testimony of the witness was prepared, and the fact that this witness is not sufficiently prepared is elucidated by the fact that he said a moment ago that this supplement refers to page 151 of the report in the Serbian, whereas here it says that this refers to page 162. So there you have it. A very simple mistake testifies to the lack of seriousness in the proceedings, and I think that is impermissible. I have absolutely no idea whether I have been provided with the complete report of this expert witness or not or rather one report is for me other type of report with the different contents is for the Trial Chamber and so on and so forth. I don't know where I stand. I don't know where I stand with respect to this report because there is so much chaos thanks to the representative of the OTP over there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The question the Trial Chamber must keep in mind is the following: The fact that this sentence was not translated into your language, did this create prejudice as far as you're concerned. Well, I didn't know that you were going to raise this question, but this morning I was looking into the comments that you gave us regarding the report, comments made by General Bozidar Delic, and on this matter General Delic made ample comments on the connection that existed between the Serbian Radical Party and the Serbian volunteers integrated into JNA units. The conclusion of the expert was discussed at length about your own expert, and therefore during cross-examination you will be able to come back to this question. Of course it is of the essence and everybody understood this, so I don't think there can be any prejudice here because this is a question of the essence. You knew exactly there was going to be mentioned in the expert's report by the Prosecution and through Judges' questions, and you can take a look at the prior transcripts. I myself dealt with this question on several occasions. So I don't -- so the fact that four lines were not disclosed in due time is very regrettable, and you're very justly -- you should raise this, but I -- it is not a great prejudice to you. It's not detrimental to you, because you know this question inside out because it's at the very core of the problem. Now, regarding the Prosecutor, as you know, the Prosecution teams have changed on several occasions. There's a new team coming in, and we can't ask this new team to be, you know, as -- as ready as the other ones. Of course the Prosecutor is one and indivisible, but when you come to a new case, you can't ask someone -- the newcomer, you know, to know everything right away from the blue. And I think the Prosecutor just found this out over the weekend. He could have not just mentioned it, but being very honest and very transparent, he informed you. I think at that settles it. Let's now continue with the examination in chief and give the floor to Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, there is a formal and material side of the problem here. The formal side of the problem says that the Prosecutor has made an impermissible great mistake and it's not the only mistake with respect to this report and the testimony of this witness. Now, I'm not interested in who is personally responsible from the Prosecution. The Prosecution, as far as I'm concerned, is an institution. Whether there's Christine Dahl or some other person is immaterial as far as I'm concerned. I'm criticising the Prosecution as a body because of their impermissible actions. Now substantially and materially you're saying I have been prejudiced. Well, let me tell you, Mr. President, that I can examine this witness in cross-examination even if I had not received a single letter of the report. I understand the material better than the Prosecution expert witness, so there's no doubt that this will not prevent me from cross-examining this witness. However, I don't think there's any reason for seeking justification all the time for the representatives of the OTP, of the Prosecution. There are many of them, many people in the prosecution they have been preparing for this five years I have not been preparing for this for five years I started preparing only when I was provided with the evidence pursuant to 65 ter those exhibits and that was in October. And you know full well that I received the report of this witness late. So they had five years. I did not have five years. They are muddling through it. I have not been muddling through anything thus far. So that's the crux of the matter. And I'd like to ask you to force the Prosecution to avoid making mistakes of that kind and to tackle this job more seriously. As far as I'm concerned, I will do my job successfully even if I don't receive any documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. What you have said is now on the transcript. In order to make sure this problem does not occur again, I would like Mr. Mundis to really double-check that everything that was sent in English to be translated into B/C/S and the other way around, you know, be there in order to make sure no problem crops up again. But let me restate my position. Disclosure between the two parties, between the Prosecutor and the accused, if the -- if Judges here were able to control the disclosure of documents, I think we wouldn't have this problem, but the problem was this was not set up earlier. We should -- there is no system to check whether the documents are correctly disclosed between the parties. Of course if Judges had a role to play here they would have been there to check that the report in English had been fully translated. Unfortunately, this is not the avenue that had been adopted at the time, and that is the way it is, and now we have to live with it. But it -- I just hope at that everyone tries to solve this at their own level. Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Thanks to the very efficient assistance ever our case manager I'm able to inform Your Honours that the statement that the accused mentions of 8th of March was disclosed on the 7th of January by our receipt number 153. So the statement that has been requested has actually been disclosed and we'll disclose it again if that facility states matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: In a language the accused under stands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Which language.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... [overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, that simply isn't true. I was given that statement only in English, and as soon as it arrived I gave it to my legal advisors and they looked through it thoroughly. They established that there were three prior statements in Serbian plus that one only in English. If the Prosecution has it in Serbian, then the problem is they didn't give it to me in Serbian. I think it is high time for you to instruct the Prosecution to never, ever again give me anything in English. I keep writing to the OTP, to Mrs. Christine Dahl, about this. Little time passes and then they again give me something in English on all subjects. This time it was only in English as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Marcussen, in the receipt is there B/C/S mentioned? We'll take a look, please. Over here, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My colleague has the language a little bit. It says that in this document there is no mention of the month of March.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not really sure, but on the first line -- first line of the third paragraph I see "December." So where is there a reference to the statement of March? Could you please show me where this is stated?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, the -- there are two -- these what we call ERN numbers mentioned. There are two statements mentioned, and the one that begins -- the second item that begins with B/C/S and then there's a number correspond to the B/C/S translation of the statement in question. And I'll try to have the statement itself printed out. Your Honours if -- Your Honours I have it here a B/C/S version of the statement and if you compare the numbers you'll see this is what has been can give it to the accused straight away so he has another copy of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, so there is a reference number B/C/S 03630263, 03650268. And it seems that this figure correspond to the B/C/S translation. I think the best is to hand it over to Mr. Seselj. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And now that we have the usher on her feet, maybe I could ask for the distribution of this. Your Honours, we have prepared a little table of conversion of page numbers because there are big differences between the page numbers of Mr. Theunens' report in English and in the language of the accused. So just for reference purposes, here's a little table that enable everyone to cross-reference the two versions. And this -- and this version has been also for future reference uploaded into e-court as 65 ter number 2854E, like "Echo." So this is just to assist everyone hopefully.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Theunens, last week we ended the examination on the issue of the acceptance of volunteers by -- by various structures of the SFRY and the Republic of Serbia, and you testified that volunteers were supported by the MUP and the Ministry of Defence of Serbia. Just to recapsulate, am I correct that basically the SFRY armed forces came to accept the incorporation of volunteers and volunteer units into its formations?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours. What we see is that through these decisions, 18th of August, 1991, Republic of Serbia decree on registration of volunteers into the TO. Then in September 1991, an instruction from the SSNO for the acceptance of volunteers into the JNA and then last but not least the 10th of December order for the engagement of volunteers in the SFRY armed forces during an imminent threat of war. And this was a SFRY Presidency order. So these decisions are intended to regularise the situation that is already existing in the field both in order to ensure the subordination of the volunteers to the SFRY armed forces as well as to regularise the status of these volunteers, because by participating in the conflict, they would be entitled to certain benefits, also compensation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, the three documents that the witness has just referred to are included in binder 1 of the material that we have received. They have Rule 65 ter number -- the first one has Rule 65 ter number 438. The second one have 65 ter number 485, and the third one has Exhibit number 7 -- sorry, 65 ter number 779. The documents are described in detail in the expert's report, and I would seek them admitted, but of course if Your Honours would like, we can take a look at the documents. I'm a bit at Your Honours' disposal on this issue. They are in -- it's about the middle of binder 1 you will find these documents. And maybe in e-court we could call up 65 ter number 438. It's already up. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have an objection. I believe that each of these documents has to be identified clearly and that the Prosecution expert has to say exactly what he thinks of each of them. Speaking of the first one, 483, we see that it's a decree about the inscription of volunteers into Territorial Defence. That's a decree of the government of the Republic of Serbia. It has nothing to do -- it can have nothing to do with the volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party. It refers to any volunteer who comes to the staff of Territorial Defence and enrolls. All this has to be clarified with this witness. I cannot waste time on it in cross-examination. It is the duty of the Prosecutor to explain every document here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Prosecution this document 483 what binder is it in.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: It is 438. If I said 483 then I was mistaken. It's 438.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Marcussen, I've found the document. It's a decree on the registration of volunteers in Territorial Defence. The best would probably be to ask the witness whether he knows this document. He can say, "Yes, I used it in -- to prepare my expert report," and then you can ask for the document to be admitted but, we need the witness -- in the minimum we need the witness to tell us that he is aware of this document, that he knows this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, have you used this decree in your report?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And in brief what -- what does this document show?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document starts with a short definition of the concept of volunteers which is in line with what we discussed earlier. It also explains then the procedure that will be applied to register these volunteers, and there's no mention made of any party affiliation. So to register these volunteers into the TO of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And so, Your Honours, I'd like to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number [overlapping speakers] Your Honours, Exhibit Number P202. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a question, Witness. I do not understand how in August 1991 registration could take place within the TO. You said that right after that in September 1991 they were included into the JNA. Then in December 1991, a few months later, they were -- there was the acceptance of the armed forces of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. Therefore, I find these three decrees, these three documents, rather strange.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, in the preparation of this report, I have tried to locate documents that would indicate to what extent this first decree was being implemented or not, and I haven't found any document to that effect. Now, that doesn't mean that such documents do not exist. However, there may also be political reasons for this first decree, because maybe it was an attempt by the authorities of the Republic of Serbia to show that actually they stand behind the concept of volunteers. What is strange then, as you have pointed out, that this decree is adopted in August even though it is only in October that one of the conditions for deployment of volunteers and for the registration of volunteers is fulfilled; and I mean by that that it's only on the 3rd of October, 1991, that the SFRY Presidency declares or observes the existence of a state of immanent threat of war, whereas in Article 3 of the decree we are discussing this conditions is explicitly discussed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I'm listening to your explanations and the questions put to you by my colleague and I'm having a close look at this document signed on the 14th of August, 1991, and following Article 2 I understand the following: Apparently people are asked to register in the Territorial Defence if they have a special status. By that I mean persons who do not have a military obligation. And there's also an age-related condition that is applied here. We have the age of 17 mentioned. In this article we can see that the following persons can be considered as volunteers. All men who are conscripts, and this applies to both men and women but who do not have a specific assignment to a specific unit. As a result, all those who have not been signed to a particular unit may register with the Territorial Defence. Witness, was that the system in place at the time? In other words, were there registers at the Territorial Defence where volunteers were registered if they fulfilled the conditions set out at Article 2.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, this decree only deals with the TO of the Republic of Serbia. So it's not for the TOs of the whole SFRY. In addition, the conditions you have read out are actually nothing more than a -- than a further specification of the conditions that were explained in Article 119 of the 1982 All People's Defence Law, which you can find in -- on page -- English page 9 of the report, meaning that volunteers are people without military obligations. Now, obviously people with military obligations, conscripts or reservists, they would always be registered. Here we see an initiative to register those who do not have military obligations. I have not been able to determine whether this was, in military terms --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me interrupt you. I'm sorry, I do not agree with you. Please have a look at Article 2 of this document. [In English] Conscription. [Interpretation] So here we have registration of people subject to military conscription. By definition these people are military people but they have not received any kind of assignment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah. That is correct, Your Honour. I should have been more specific. I was looking at it in the context of the mobilisations that were ongoing and especially from the month of September onwards. Yes, indeed we see an initiative to register those who have basically not received wartime assignments in the JNA or who have no military obligations any more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're talking about an initiative here, talking about this document, but let's assume for one minute that this situation had prevailed before in the 1970s, in the 1980s, that automatically Territorial Defence units were supposed to have registers where people -- whereby people were in a position to volunteer, because before making statements, we have to make sure that this is a unique situation. I am not in a position to check that, but you -- you seem to be saying that this situation was out of the ordinary. But you never know. This might have been something quite usual.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, based on the review I've done and I mean the documents I've seen, this is an unusual situation, because there was no requirement to register volunteers in the TO unless you do that in view of your assessment of future developments where when a certain situation arises where there is an urgent need for those volunteers that you want as a pre-emptive move register them already before such a development arises. But again referring to Article 119 of the 1982 All People's Defence Law, there is no information on the specific modalities for registration or enrollment of volunteers into the armed forces. The article specifies the three conditions but also says that in time of peace volunteers can join the armed forces to participate in military exercises.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Witness, but here at the top of this decree I see that mention is made to Article 2, item 2, and Article 30, paragraph 1, on the law on the government of the Republic of Serbia. Are you aware of that article? This decree has been passed as a result of this law and of this paragraph apparently.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm not familiar with the specific details of the legal references you have mentioned but I would conclude -- I would assume that they deal with the formal aspects and the aspect to issue this particular decree as defence matters are dealt with in the Law on Defence of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Before we move on, I'd like to follow up on the question put by Mr. Seselj in relation to the volunteers who were registered with the Territorial Defence. Do you know if any volunteers were seeking registration with the TO by some sort of invitation from the political parties?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have not come across such information. The -- the role of -- actually, when political parties become involved, it's they who are -- who are recruiting the volunteers. But as we see --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Who is "they"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry, the political parties like the Serbian Radical Party, the Serbian Renewal Movement. And what I've seen in such documents I included in the report that in the case of the Serbian Radical Party, there are contacts with the Serbian Ministry of Defence, for example, to organise the payment of the volunteers. As I mentioned earlier, the registration is -- is an important legal measure, because if a volunteer goes somewhere in Croatia to participate in the fighting, well, he has to quit his job or at least has to be an arrangement with his job if he had a job. If he gets injured, then there's to be some compensation. If he gets killed, well, maybe his relatives are entitled to certain benefits, and without registration there cannot be such benefits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: True, but the issue is if you have any evidence of the involvement of the political parties in the recruitment of volunteers to the TO.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, Your Honours. The documents I reviewed indicate that the SRS volunteers or the volunteers that are being recruited by the SRS are sent as separate, as they call it, detachments or groups to the battlefield where they continue to have their own insignia or own structure linking them to the Serbian Radical Party. There are examples of JNA documents where they, for example, mention that an SRS volunteer who was part of a JNA unit, apparently not a separate detachment, was injured, but he's still identify as an SRS volunteer, not as a volunteer or a recruit -- or a conscript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: So are you saying that to the extent in which SRS volunteers actually did register formally with the TO, they did so on an individual basis? Is that what you're saying? So that we cannot see in the registration whether any of the volunteers were linked somehow to the political parties, including the SRS.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, the documents I have seen indicate that SRS volunteers register with the SRS, with the political party. Whether there was a subsequent registration with the Territorial Defence, I cannot say because I haven't seen these documents. The SRS, as is indicated in my report, keeps records of the volunteers that have registered with them indicating or suggesting that actually the SRS is doing the same thing as the recruitment officers or registration officers would normally do. As I mentioned, they are involved in the payment of the volunteers in connection with the Serbian Ministry of Defence. Now, I don't want to complicate matters, but some of these volunteers when they are sent to the battlefield they become part of the local Serb Territorial Defence. So in addition to the detachments I mentioned in -- in my previous reply, when we look at Western Slavonia, we see that local Serb TO in Western Slavonia, in the various areas, actually consist to -- to a certain large or small extent of SRS volunteers who are then considered members of the local Serb TO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I think we should leave it to the Prosecution to continue now. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I don't know if it is -- sorry?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Before I give the floor to Mr. Marcussen, I have an additional question. You have a theory about these groups of volunteers, these grouped volunteers. I'm not going to go into your theories. I'm just looking at the document. And if I look at this document, what do I see? I see that this decree of the 14th of August, 1991, no mention is ever made of the involvement of political parties. There of could been an additional article, Article 10 or Article X stating that as part of this registration of volunteers political parties are invited to send their volunteers, and nothing of the kind can be found in this document. But if you have a look at this document, at the end of the document you find that there is a form here at the end for the registration of a volunteer with the date of birth, the place of residence, the identity card number, and then the volunteer's supposed to write in the date and to sign this form. We are talking, therefore, about individual registration and not of grouped -- group registration. At no point in this document is there a mention of a political party, of a group-type registration. I'm sure you've seen this document at the end, this sort of form at the end.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours. To start with the last part your comment, it is -- as I mentioned, I think, last week, it is only in the SFRY Presidency order of the 10th of December that mention is made of volunteer formations. And it's obviously also a correct observation of the Presiding Judge that this decree does not make mention of political parties. But if you allow me, I would like to draw your attention to page 53, English page 53 in part 2 of the report. This is in the section where I discuss the activities of the SRS War Staff, in particular the relations the SRS War Staff maintains with its volunteers. In the middle of the page there is a title 5: "Record-keeping by the SRS War Staff on SRS/SCP volunteers." And I quote Mr. Seselj there from an interview he gives in November 1991, which is actually included in one of his books published in 1993, and the actual interview corresponds with 65 ter number 750, and there Mr. Seselj says: "We keep a neat record of all those who have been sent to the battlefield, of how long they stayed on the battlefield, under which circumstances, and which battles they participated in, and all the rest." So basically we see that the Serbian Radical Party is doing similar activities as according to the decree we were discussing should normally have been done by the authorities, by the Ministry of Defence or its subordinate officers all over the territory of the Republic of Serbia. On the next page, English page 54, I have shown -- I have included certain certificates that were issued by the Radical Party or the War Staff to volunteers, to SRS volunteers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, just to maybe clarify the terminology. When you talk about recruitment and registration, what exactly do you mean?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean by that that the procedure to -- when a person who declares himself a volunteer presents himself, that he is registered into -- as far as the decree is concerned into the TO of the Republic of Serbia. So as the Presiding Judge mentioned, certain information will be taken. There will also be certain checks to see whether the person has a criminal record or not, medical checks to see which military duties the volunteer can carry out or not and so on and so on, and then a file is constituted which will then serve in order it assign this volunteer once he has been accepted, to assign him to a particular unit where there is a requirement for manpower on an individual basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And would I be correct in suggesting that you are saying that that is different from the issue of the deployment of the volunteers and their resubordination maybe to various JNA units or their deployment under a TO in some region?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours. This is -- the deployment is the next step, and following from my previous answer, using SFRY legislation as the basis for my reply, volunteers would, after registration, be deployed to units where that is need for such individuals. For example, if there is an artillery unit which has a lack of -- of gunners, well -- and we see we have a number of people who volunteer and they have the right background and they have the right military training, they will be sent to that artillery unit then. One element I didn't mention is between the registration and the deployment there can also be training -- or there should be training and that will depend of the experience of the particular volunteer and also the requirements of the units to which this particular volunteer or -- will be sent.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, if we could then briefly look at the next exhibit, which is 65 ter number 485. This is an instruction on accepting volunteers into the Yugoslav national army, JNA from the federal secretariat for national defence. This document is cited or quoted in extenso in part 1, page 89 of the expert report. That will be page 94 in B/C/S. Mr. Theunens, very briefly what -- what role does this document play in your report?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have included this instruction, Your Honours, for the same reasons that I have included the decree of the government of the Republic of Serbia with the difference that here we're talking about the acceptance of volunteers into the JNA. The instruction then mentions the conditions, I mean, defines volunteers and mentions the conditions under which volunteers can be accepted and also describes the procedure that will be applied between when the moment that the volunteer presents himself to a recruitment office and the moment of his deployment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, I'd like to ask for an exhibit number for this. I ask this be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number P203.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And now the third document that we talked about, 65 ter number 779 is referred to part 1 of the expert report page 92 and that will be in B/C/S page 96. Mr. Theunens, I believe that in your report you point out a change in -- in the status of volunteers in this particular document. Could you briefly explain us what -- why that document is significant?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document is significant, Your Honours, because it is the first document, or the first legal document that mentions the concept of volunteer formations and that is done in paragraph or Article 7 of the order. And even if I -- if I can read it out, it talks about volunteer formations currently engaged outside the armed forces which as I commented in the report is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, sorry for interrupting, but I do not agree with you, because in the decree dated 14th of August, 1991, it was stated that in peacetime it was possible to organise formations and to conduct exercises together with the army. Therefore, what you've just said is completely contrary to what we see in the decree of the 14th of August, 1991, where such formations were already provided for. It is provided for at Article 3, penultimate paragraph of Article 3. In peacetime.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Maybe -- maybe there's a translation issue, Your Honours, but as I read Article 3 of the August 1991 decree, it states -- it states that in peacetime and for training purposes persons from Article 2 of this decree can voluntarily join the military manoeuvres and other forms of training of the units, headquarters, and institutions of Territorial Defence. The reference to units here is to units of the Territorial Defence, whereas in the 10th of December residency order mention is made of volunteer formations engaged outside the armed forces. The TO is one of the two components of the SFRY armed forces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, quite so. You're right. But in terms of training, in terms of formation, as of the month of August any volunteer, whether belonging to the JNA or the TO of the federal army, that volunteer had the possibility of receiving training. That's what I wanted to outline, to stress. Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I would like to tender 65 ter number 779.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number P204.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd now like to move on to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment, please. At this stage of the presentation of your case I have one question in order to avoid any confusion. At the time, Witness, one could be a volunteer with the TO, with the JNA, or with the federal army; is that correct? And the federal army was the JNA, of course.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, and that was actually what was already explained in Article 119 of the 1982 All People's Defence Law. However, as paragraph 7 of this December 1991 SFRY Presidency order shows, there is actually a third option that exists, namely volunteer formations currently engaged outside the armed forces. And the article continues: "They are carrying out certain military assignments." The next paragraph of Article 7 supports the conclusion that in addition to volunteers in the JNA and the TO, we have also other volunteers, because at second paragraph states that all individuals and volunteer formations not included in the armed forces of the SFRY, in the manner defined this order, shall be removed from the territory, and then it's further explained which territory. I would also like to draw your attention to paragraph 8 of that order, the SFRY Presidency order of 10th of December, which states that: "Lawful measures will be taken against persons found wearing uniforms and insignia of members of the SFRY armed forces who have not joined the armed forces of the SFRY in a way defined by law or regulated their position in accordance with this order."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as you're concerned, who are these volunteers who are outside? Who are these people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, these are the people who are actually discussed in -- further on in this -- or a bit earlier in this section. These are namely people who are part of other formations, sometimes -- I mean, some are called Serbian guard. Others are called -- call themselves Chetniks detachment. There is a group that calls itself Dusan Silni. There are also groups known as Arkan Tigers or Dragan's men. So various groups who are present on -- in the conflict zone and carry out certain operations there. Most of them are subordinated to the JNA, but from the documents one can see at that there are sometimes problems with this subordination, and even when these groups are formally subordinated to the JNA, they may pursue their own agenda. Just to finalise, in the report I also explain that people like Arkan and Dragan, and that starts on page 80, English page 80, part 1 of the report, Arkan and Dragan they based on information intelligence collected by the military security organs enjoy particular relations with the Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Serbia at the time of the events described in the report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I've understood you correctly, these volunteer formations that are not part of the Serbian armed forces, these would be paramilitary units.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour if you define paramilitary units by units not foreseen in the law but who are carrying out military activities and who are organised in military fashion, then I agree with you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These formations are operating in non-compliance with this law. In other words, in an illegal fashion if we bear in mind this order.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's important to take into account that this order dates from the 10th of December, which is when you look at the context of the conflict fairly late. I remember from the testimony of General Vasiljevic in the Milosevic trial that when he visited the Vukovar battlefield in November he noticed some of these groups, and he was the chief of the security administration within the SSNO, he felt the need to do something about it so he wrote a document to the federal secretary for People's Defence, Kadijevic, who then forwarded the information to the SFRY Presidency in order to have something done about the situation. And that can explain that this order is fairly late, 10th of December. So it can only have effect for the future. And as you see in paragraph 7, the last line that the order takes effect within ten days of the order taking -- sorry, I mean paragraph 7 has to be complied with within ten days after the order coming into effect, and the order comes into effect on the 10th of December, 1991. So the order cannot address the situation that existed before, but the fact that this is -- aspect is explicitly mentioned in the order indicates that there was a problem. I mean, the aspect of volunteer formations operating outside the SFRY armed forces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is an essential issue we are discussing. This text which is dated of December 1991, you seem to establish a connection between this document and the Vukovar events, and on listening to you I was wondering whether this was not a way of regulating with hindsight the existence of some of the units that had been on the battlefield. So you are the expert. As far as regulating the presence of paramilitary units, what is your feeling about this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I agree with you. That is exactly the measure that has been taken. I was browsing through my report for -- there's a famous -- or it became famous, a letter by the assistant commander for morale of the 1st Proletarian Guards Mechanised Division, which was a unit which was active in Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem south of Vukovar and their Colonel Eremija, the letter dates from October talks about crimes committed by for example Dusan Silni as well as other groups, and in his letter, Eremija suggests or asks the government of the Republic of Serbia as well as the military authorities to act against such groups. So this again indicates that there were groups operating which were not subordinated or at least which even when they were subordinated or admitted by the JNA commander in the area who is responsible then for his own responsibility and who committed crimes and there was a lack of action in that situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, in military terms the scope of Article 7, does this not mean that these volunteer formations that were paramilitary unit are as of the date of this order placed under the control of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honour, but if you allow me, I will clarify. During operations each commander has his zone of responsibility as the term explains he is responsible for what's happening in that area and in the JNA it was called zone of operations but its the same concept. So the commander is the only one who can issue orders, and he's -- as I said, he's responsible. Now, if there are formations in that zone which are not subordinated to him, he has to take measures to subordinate them, which is also explained in this order, or to remove them, but he cannot allow that there are groups active there doing certain things whereby these groups are not subordinated to him because that creates chaos. So to answer your question, at the latest, ten days after the 10th of December, all volunteer formations have to be subordinated to the JNA or they have to be removed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, thank you. I propose now to move to a different topic, namely --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry. Before you move on to another topic, I would like to know whether the Arkan's and Dragan's volunteers, according to your knowledge, after December 1991, whether these units were placed under the JNA or the Yugoslav armed forces.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the activities of the Arkan volunteers or Arkan's Tigers, also known as the Serbian Volunteer Guard, are explained in the section on Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem in part 2 of the report, as well in the section on volunteers we are discussing, and as far as Arkan is concerned --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Given that we don't know whether we are going to admit the report into evidence, could you please explain this to us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. So Arkan's volunteers or the Serbian Volunteer Guard are active in the zone of responsibility of operation group north in Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem, which is the area north of the Vuka river by the Vuka cuts Vukovar in two parts. From the information given by the commander of the 1st Military District was the overall commander in the area, both of Operational Group north as well as operational group south. He stated that everybody, including Arkan's Serbian Volunteer Guard were subordinated to him. However, on the lower level, and I've quoted a number of reports by security organs of the JNA, there were sometimes problems between JNA units in the area and Arkan where -- whereby, for example, these lower-level security organs say, "Look. Arkan has no respect for the JNA. He's committing crimes. He's involved in smuggling and looting, and we have no control." I've also quoted in the report an excerpt from a statement General Andrija Biorcevic, the commander of the 12th Novi Sad Corps and the commander of OG North; for the transcript 12th Novi Sad Corps, and commander of OG north, made in January 1992 for the local TV where he said, and I'm paraphrasing him, he said: "Some people call the Arkan Tigers paramilitaries." He then says these are not paramilitaries. They are actually good soldiers because they continue when other soldiers refuse to carry on. And then so he says we first show the area, and then the Arkan Tigers enter in order to kill those who do not wish to surrender. For what Dragan is concerned, Dragan had a training centre it or established a training centre in Golubic, which is near Knin, and that's in a totally different part of Croatia. It's in the Krajina. A training centre where members of the police of Mr. Martic were trained. According to a document I included in my report, the security administration of the SSNO had intelligence that this camp -- or that Dragan was supported by Jovica Stanisic and Frenki Simatovic who were two senior officials of the state security of the Republic of Serbia in establishing and managing organising that training centre. And this document is 65 ter number 457, which you can find on page 80, part 1 of the report, English page 80.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Witness. Now, when you answered this question, you raise another issue. Captain Dragan, who seemingly was in contact with Simatovic and Stanisic. These people are in fact working for the Ministry of the Interior, not for the Ministry of Defence. With this text we have in front us, the armed forces are mentioned, the armed forces of the federal republic. Do these armed forces also include the units of the MUP? And if that is the case, who is the Supreme Commander?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours. I understand the question. Your question is basically answered by Article 104 of the 1982 All People's Defence Law which you can find on page 10 of part 1 of the report when I discuss the participation of the police in combat operations, and the article, I summarise it, states that if in one of the three states, so the police is carrying out military tasks for the armed forces, they were placed under the authorised officer who direction military activities. And that would be in most cases a JNA officer. Now, the law is of course a de jure -- addresses the de jure situation. The unit of Dragan or Arkan, these are obviously de facto units, but we see -- and that's also something I have tried to show throughout the report, that efforts are undertaken to legalise a de facto situation when this de facto situation does not correspond which what has been foreseen by the -- in the de jure context.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Marcussen, I really apologise for this, but could you elicit from the witness, and I'll leave it to you, then, to tell us whether the December order was effectively implemented vis-a-vis the volunteer groups outside the armed forces? I think this was the crux of Judge Lattanzi's question also, but I'm not sure of the answer that the witness gave.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honour. We will -- we will come back to the situation in Croatia and Bosnia-Herzegovina in more detail later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: But I do think it is a good idea, maybe, Mr. Theunens, if you could answer in brief this question. Based on the material you have reviewed from the conflict in Croatia and in Bosnia, were this December decree actually implemented?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, for what Croatia is concerned I can be brief because the conflict was more or less finished by then. I have seen one document which is the western Slavonia section which covers the situation in December in the area where the JNA commander in the area says, "Look, the volunteers were not part of my formation." I haven't seen a second document to counter that. For what Bosnia-Herzegovina is concerned, I can maybe reply with one example, Bijeljina, when Arkan Tigers participated in the takeover the city, the JNA corps commander of the 17th Corps rights in his report to his superiors that Arkan does not allow the JNA tanks to enter the city, so this would suggest or this indicated actually the order was not implemented in Bijeljina. I apologise if I'm sometimes a bit extensive but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, Mr. Theunens mentioned in one of his answers Exhibit number 65 ter number 457. I wondered whether we should maybe admit that into evidence now that he's described that so Your Honours can consult it when reviewing the record later on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Exhibit 457. Don't we have it?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Sorry, this particular document was not selected for the bundle of material that was included for the examination. As Your Honours know, there are about 400 documents cited in the report and we have selected around hundred just to make the exercise manageable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But we can perhaps see it on the screen, actually. Yes, it's this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: -- is this the document that you refer to?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is, Your Honours. And if you go to the end, for example, you will see the address list. So the last page. Just to show that it was a document compiled at -- bit security organs at the SSNO, and it is only released to very few people. So it says signed by Colonel Boskovic. His title is indicated on the document and it's sent to army General Kadijevic, and then there are six additional copies, which looking -- I mean from the reliability of the source and the credibility of the information, it is indeed an intelligence report, but before information is sent to actually the highest, to the highest military official, Kadijevic, the people who compiled the report have done their checks and therefore I would consider this a reliable -- a -- the information included in the report as credible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One question regarding this document. This document is addressed to General Kadijevic, and this document mentions Captain Dragan, who seemingly would be Australian and talk -- discusses his connections with the MUP. This is the conclusion -- what the conclusion of this document states. I would rightfully have a question on this issue. If Captain Dragan was part of the JNA or placed under the control of the JNA, how is it that in the army reports are drafted about him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, first a short clarification. The title or the name Captain Dragan is -- was something that was kind of invented. He was never a captain. His real name was Dragan Vasiljkovic, and if I remember well, he was a non-commissioned officer, a sergeant; but it sounded better for the media like to have the title Captain Dragan so it's just a title that he used, and he was allowed to use that by the people who controlled him. This dates from August 1991. At that moment -- for that time period I haven't seen any information indicating that Dragan was under the control or part of the armed forces. Actually, the documents shows that Dragan has close relations with senior officials of the state security of the Republic of Serbia, Stanisic and Simatovic, and also -- and that's maybe something we will see with other documents. The situation as it develops between summer 1991 and December 1991 there are more if I can call it that way de facto elements, and it seems that at the same time that, for example, Arkan is being subordinated to OG north and actually praised by the commander of OG north, Bejocevic, members of security organs of subordinate units of OG north are compiling reports highlighting actually the bad things Arkan does. So because of this de facto nature of the situation it is difficult to draw one line in, for example, the reporting that is being done.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have an objection to placing this document among the exhibits. First of all, this document shows that Captain Dragan did not form the centre for training at Golubic, and the witness said that it was established by Captain Dragan. You heard him say that a moment ago. The document shows that Captain Dragan was engaged as an instructor in the centre now the Prosecution has many documents where we see that the training centre in Golubic was established by the police of the Serbian Krajina. It's the police centre for training police training centre. Secondly, this is a document of military security which no court in Yugoslavia or in Serbia would recognise as a piece of evidence, as an exhibit. This document -- by this document a struggle is being waged against the police of Serbia because of the rivalry between two security structures, the civilian and the military; and the Prosecution has these documents, and they provided me with them; but I can't bring them all in with me. The Prosecution has documents showing that Captain Dragan was under the operative processing of the state security services of Serbia from which we can see that Klara Mandic brought him and we can see that Carla Mandic was suspected of being a Mossad spy in Belgrade. The Prosecutor has that. Ask the Prosecutor to confirm or deny that, so if he is presenting police documents, then the military security documents of the military ones and civilian ones must be shown because we have a war here between two security structures in which all foul play is allowed and you will find documents where the military service suspects me of collaborating with the civilian service and vice versa. The civilian thinks I'm working with the military whereas I was processed by both those services and the Prosecution has documents which show this, so I'm in principle against any document of the security service being entered into evidence because they are unreliable extremely so; and the military security service was most intensively under the control of the League of Communists, the movement for Yugoslavia, the generals party. So this witness is not taking that into account and the situation is highly complex. These are complicated matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, this document, you have examined this document as part of your expert report; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. It's included on page 80. And on page 81, I -- just to corroborate the information included in this report, at least the information on the links between Dragan and the state security of the Republic of Serbia I have included a letter Dragan sent on the 8th of November to the command of the TO, the Republic of Serbia, which is 65 ter number 7148, and in that letter Dragan states that he has obligations towards the state security of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry. To your knowledge between the military security service and the civilian security services was there a clash?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have not studied that issue while preparing the report. It is true through the course of 1991 but mainly in 1992, a conflict arises between, let's say, the Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Serbia on one hand and the armed forces on the other hand because in very simple terms, Mr. Milosevic, as the president of the Republic of Serbia and his de facto powers is reinforcing the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia to the detriment of the armed forces. And also certain senior generals who still believed in Yugoslavia actually noticed that Milosevic, while executing his de facto powers, is not necessarily pursuing the same goals, i.e., maintaining Yugoslavia, but was pursuing other goals, but this is really very simple overview of a very complex situation. But again, I do not think at that an alleged conflict between the Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Serbia and the state -- excuse me, the military intelligence security services had any influence on the contents of this report or orders I included in my report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Registrar, could we have a number, please, exhibit number for this document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Exhibit number P205.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In addition to the admission of this exhibit, I would like to provide the following personal view: This document is challenged by Mr. Seselj, but as far as I'm concerned, I can see that this document has indications of reliability. This was signed by someone whom one can identify. This person was part of the internal services security services of the army. The addressee is General Kadijevic. And furthermore, this document provides data and names which are at -- at the heart of these proceedings, Mr. Babic, Mr. Milosevic, Captain Dragan, which -- whose part he played in these events will be mentioned again. The War Staff. So all these items are in favour of the admission of this document. I find this relevant, but the probative value of this document will be assessed once the Trial Chamber has all the elements at hand. This is what I wished to say to avoid spending too much time on objections that could be repeated in the future. It is important to be aware of the fact when the document does have signs of reliability, there is no point of -- no point in dismissing the document. It's now time to have the break. We shall have a 20-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Let's resume, and I give the floor to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I would like now to move to the issue of the SRS/SCP. So that will be item 4 in the outline that I handed out last week. Mr. Theunens, in your binder you have 65 ter number 1990. And maybe we could call that up on the screen as well. That is the 1994 statute of the Serb Radical Party, Serbian Radical Party. You quote Article 3 of this statute in part 2, page 30, B/C/S page 133, of your report. And as the -- as the mission of the SRS, now, this particular provision is from the 1994 statute. My question is based on the material you have reviewed, have you formed an opinion about whether or not the aims were the same prior to this statute?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, formally when looking at the 1991 statute, these aims were not the same; but in practice when looking at the role of the Radical Party in the volunteers and the -- the goals these volunteers were pursuing as well as the speeches of Mr. Seselj, I would conclude that the goals as listed in the 1994 statute also existed in practice in 1991 and 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would like to request the admission of 65 ter 1990.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit P206.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But I have a question, expert, please. I was quite interested by the symbols of the party on Article 6 and 7 where we note that there is a flag that's 2 by 1 metres, that there's even a anthem, Tomo Daleko, and there are symbols. So among all these documents that you studied for these -- the volunteers that are in the TO and the JNA and the so on, could you tell us whether they had these symbols with them? Were there any banners? Did they sing their anthem? Because if we assume there is a strong connection between these volunteers and the party, then all the more. So forth fact that this would be apparent in the unit, which is why I'm asking you the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, in the report there are several documents included where JNA officers complain that the volunteers do not accept the uniform and more specifically, the five-pointed star because it's considered a symbol of Communism, and that volunteers, in particular SRS volunteers prefer to wear their own uniform and carry their own symbols. Now I have not been able to establish whether the symbols worn by the SRS volunteers were exactly the same ones as are described in Article 7. There is no uniformity in the symbols that are worn by the volunteers, in particular SRS volunteers. Some will wear the kokarda, the insignia. Come will have the fur hat, others not. Some come with a camouflage uniform which kind of looks like a camouflaged JNA uniform, others not. So it's very heterogenous.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, the witness also mentioned the 1991 statute of the SRS. It is the next tab in your binder and as the witness mentioned it has 65 ter number 169. I was not intending to really go into this document with the witness, but I was going to suggest that it be admitted into evidence nonetheless for future reference on this point. It's referred to in the report, of course, at page 30 or 133.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This document 169, did you look into it when drafting your report?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes -- yes, Your Honour, but I haven't included it in the report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but you did look into it. Therefore could we have a number please, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number P207.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, the next series of exhibits in your binders that I'm going to go through I would like to request that we deal with in private session. On the 2nd of October, 2006, Trial Chamber I rendered a decision on Prosecution's motion concerning filing of expert report with confidential annex and ex parte annexes. The decision granted the prosecution, the late disclosure of Mr. Theunens' report and also held that the report, if admitted should be filed under seal, the unredacted report should be filed under seal, and the public will only have access to a redacted version of the report. That is because a lot of the material referred to comes from sensitive sources and the documents that I'm going to go through are going to come -- are the same documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This deals with the witnesses that have been granted protective measures or documents for which -- that come under Rule 70, is that it?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: They are witnesses who have protective measures in this case indeed, and, yes, the documents have been sensitive and there is a concern that revealing to the public the source of these documents could put them in danger.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Then we want to deal with this now. So let's move to private session for a few minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're now in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are in open session. Please ask your question to the witness, Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, could you explain to us what this document is? Who is it from, for a start?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, that is document from the command of the 1st military district. If we could move to the last page we could see who signed it, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: We can take a look at that. And what -- what is the contents of this document?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The contents of the document actually it's the assistant commander for morale and legal affairs or the 1st Military District who informs the subordinate units of the 1st Military District command of the military implications of the establishment of the state of imminent threat of war by the SFRY Presidency and this decision is mentioned in the first paragraph of the document on page 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, could we go back to page 1, please.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: First paragraph. So the decision of the SFRY Presidency of 03 October 1991 establish the existence of an imminent threat of war -- imminent or immediate threat of war in the country, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And the particular report is the same -- or the information is sent out on the 7th of October.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I'd like to tender that into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours -- Your Honours, Exhibit number P209.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And for the reasons already mentioned, we'll then need to go back into private session for the continuation of the testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One comment before we do so. This document is dated October 7. The proclamation of the immediate threat of war, dated from the 3rd of October, 1991, and so far we haven't seen that document, have we?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, we haven't, Your Honours. I'm just looking whether I quoted it in my report, but I -- no, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's a vital document. It's a document that lays at the very heart of this issue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since we don't have this in the binder, I demand that the Prosecution give me that document immediately in Serbian. I can't just look for it in my cell. The Prosecution is duty-bound to deliver in binders all the documents they intend to handle in cross -- in their examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could your case manager look for this document, document of October 3rd, 1991? It should be there somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, two things. One, we will provide the accused with a printout of the document we're seeing on the screen. Two, we will see if we have this document -- I mean, the Prosecution doesn't have every single military document that have been issued, so I'm not sure whether we actually have that document in our evidence collection; but we'll make an effort to see if we can find it and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. We'll hand over this document to Mr. Seselj right now.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And one more thing, Mr. President. I know for certain that the Prosecution has the set of documents of the SFRY Official Gazettes of 1991 and the decision to proclaim a state of imminent -- an emergency threat of war. It was probably published in the Official Gazette and they have it all if they take the trouble to find it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You should have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I'm grateful to the accused for his assistance in this matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. We'll receive this document later. Let's go back into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're now in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: What I presuppose to do, Your Honours, is I will adjust my examination so that we try not to reveal any confidential details about this so we avoid going in and out of private session, which means it will be a little more rudimentary what I will do with the documents, but maybe as these documents are described elsewhere we can proceed in this manner. And to ensure the confidentiality, the documents themselves, I believe, are not going to be broadcast. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, is this a document you referred to in your report?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, I do, on page 36 in the second part of the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And am I correct in stating that this document illustrates a change in the composition of the War Staff in December 1991?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Actually, Your Honours, the document provides an overview of the members of the War Staff, whereby it also includes information on the, if I can call it that way, the peacetime occupations of the members, their position in the War Staff, as well as their participation in the conflict, more specifically in Croatia, if there is such participation.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, objection. Where does it say here that this is a list of the War Staff, a document of the War Staff? It just says "List" here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, the title is "List." There's nothing else.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honours, but when you go through the document you will see that at the end of each paragraph where the duties of the various people are explained, it says for the first person "Chief of the War Staff," the second, "Deputy chief of the War Staff," and I can continue. So for various people, in total nine individuals, it mentions what their position in the War Staff is. There may be other members of the War Staff, but again looking in context with the previous documents we looked at, this allows me to conclude that this is indeed a list of the SRS War Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, this -- this document has been --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection. Mr. President, I think that you have to intervene at this point just for three persons from this list does it say -- or rather just two persons does it say that they are members of the War Staff? Whereas where the third is concerned, we knew from a series of documents that he was a member the War Staff. As to the rest, there's no data. So I think that you must step in. You must intervene here. They must tell you what this document means.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, in this list there is somebody who is the head of this, and there is his deputy, and then we can see that the other members hold administrative positions involved in logistics, in secretarial work, and so on and so forth. So we are under the impression that we have a list here which is -- refers to an entity involved in logistical and administrative matters. The fact that two people here are qualified as War Staff or deputy War Staff that's true, but for the others, it seems to be more of an administrative role. Wouldn't this list be a component of two institutions?
