One would be the SRS with the Administrative Services and something specific about it, because this -- this crisis cell would then have become the War Staff. You then conclude that this entire list refers to the War Staff members.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours. Now, that we've seen when discussing military structures in the military staff there is also an administrative part. And I wouldn't really consider this document as to the -- from the quantitative aspect if it says for five or six people there are administrative officers, I wouldn't necessarily draw the conclusion then, Okay this has to be an administrative body, because in particular the three first people on the list the names are also given -- were also given in 65 ter number 534 and 536, and there's a clear linkage with the SRS War Staff. There's no doubt that the War Staff, as any other staff, includes also administrative personnel.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, did you also in your report discuss, I believe in a part, the use of military-type titles within the War Staff and within the SRS? Is the document also relevant in that context?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is relevant, in particular for the three first persons. There's a chief of the War Staff, there's a deputy chief, and there's a logistics commander.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, you are a military expert. I'm sure you were struck like I was by the stamp we can see on the document in B/C/S. That is stamp here, and this stamp, when translated into English says "Main Board of the SRS." Now, in military terms, if this War Staff has existed, then there would have been the War Staff stamp or military -- or War Staff would have been on the document. We have the feeling that this is the stamp of the SRS which is used in all cases.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honours, it's a stamp of the Radical Party most likely an authenticated document. Now when we review the other documents on the SRS War Staff, including my report, they are not always as consistent as one would expect from military documents in the layout. Sometimes the heading says SRS War Staff. Here the heading says Serbian Radical Party. So it is not as -- as well organised as a military organisation based on documents I reviewed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As you a military analyst, as you have been working for years for the OTP, and as in addition you have testified in a number of cases, I'm sure that you were struck by the fact that this document bears a number which is 0512-7-91. Did you ever ask yourself whether this was a general number that recorded the document? Was this being registered by the president of the party, the vice-president of the party, or just a typical War Staff registration number? No, you didn't question that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I tried to establish what I would call a logic in -- when comparing the various War Staff and Radical Party documents we had, but I'm not able to draw any conclusions to that effect. The only thing one can conclude from this report is that it's signed by the chief of the SRS War Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're not answering my question. I addressed myself to the military analyst. You are such a military analyst. You know as well as I do that in the former Yugoslavia all the armies or the way in which the army operated. Operation on the basis of registration numbers, and with these registration numbers we have dates and we have figures which are evocative, which explain that such-and-such an order, such a such a document pertains to a particular topic, a particular area and so on and so forth. It would have been interesting to discover as far as in document is concerned whether you attribute to the War Staff, whether the registration number is a specific War Staff number or whether it is a more general number. Or perhaps it might be the 512th document of the SRS in 1991, or because of the figure 1 we have this might have been the first document of the War Staff. Maybe you didn't think about it, but I have.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I understand your question, and maybe I misexpressed myself, but I tried to draw a similar conclusion as you did to see whether the numbers allow to draw conclusions, but I have not been able to draw such a conclusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So you were unable to. Fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, this particular document has been marked for identification as P24 at this stage as it's referred to in the report and has been discussed there. I would respectfully request that it be admitted as such.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this brings us to the question of relevance. A document that nobody seems to be able to identify as to what it means and what it represents and when it was compiled, for what reason, for what purpose, then how can it be said to be relevant and to be admitted at all? Of course I don't mind that it is admitted, but this is an objection of principle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The relevance pertains to the SRS, because the SRS is mentioned in the indictment. So there is here a modicum of relevance. What we will do in the future with this document I don't know. This is something which we will see at the end of the day. So let's have a P24 let's give it a number which was marked for identification will be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But, Mr. President, if I don't explain what this document means to you, who's going to explain it? There's nobody that can explain the document except me, and I'm not going to do it now. I'm not going to explain the document now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You may do it during cross-examination or you can address this matter again and address the document again during the cross-examination and say to the witness, "We have a document with a list," and so on and so forth. Please proceed, Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit number P24 under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And I was alerted to the fact that I did not ask specifically for P10 and 11 -- sorry, P210 and 211 to be placed under seal. I was in the mode of private session from before. So I'd like to ask that these two exhibits be admitted under seal, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P210 and P211, registrar, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. It's duly noted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, in addition to the War Staff, were there other parts of the SRS that became involved in recruiting and dispatching volunteers? And I'm thinking particular in the context of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a document included in the report, a report by -- or the document is by Colonel Tolimir, chief of the intelligence security administration of the VRS where he talks about the role of the Serbian Radical Party in Bosnia-Herzegovina in the recruitment of volunteers.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, if you would follow me to the next tab where we have Exhibit number 65 ter 796.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I'll ask first, Mr. Theunens, is this a document that you have looked at in your report?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours. And this document mentions the same individual, Nikodin Cavic, as is also identified in the report by Colonel Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And -- and this document, Your Honour, is as you can see a request from the War Staff that this person sign up volunteers for the more effective dispatchment of volunteers. I would like to request the admission of this document as well, Your Honours, under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 212 under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Next if we could call up Exhibit number 65 ter 1974. And this particular document can be shown to the public. Your Honours, that is published -- a document published by the SRS. And if we look at the second page of the English translation, you will see that it is a document which addresses what is called the basic military organisation of the Serbian Radical Party volunteers. And what I would like to ask the witness about is on page 3 if you would follow me there and it's page 2 and 3 in the B/C/S version for the accused?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection. Mr. President, the Prosecutor is duty-bound to identify this document. He just said one thing and that is that the document was published by the Serbian Radical Party but he has to tell us what the Serbian Radical Party published. Is it a party document or did the party publish it as somebody's book with an author? So you must know what this is about. You must be told that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Marcussen, at the time you were saying that I had the same question. Where does this document come from? Do you have any information about it?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honour. I don't have it in memory, though. Actually, maybe the witness might remember the particular source of this document.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. This document was published in part 10 of the book in Sinisa Aksentijevic, "Philippics Lens of Chetniks Vojvoda," which was authored by Vojislav Seselj and published in 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, on page 3 of the document there is a --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have here that book and you can see the book is by Sinisa Aksentijevic who's there, and the title is Dr. Vojislav Seselj in the camera lens of Aksentijevic and it's the "Philippics Lens of the Chetniks Vojvoda." So it is not a book by me it's a book about me written by Sinisa Aksentijevic based on his articles that he wrote, quotations from my public appearances, questions he asked me, and certain other documents that he published so I have to intervene there to put that right because I don't want the Trial Chamber or the public to be misled.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, on listening to your line 16 and 17 of page 77, I had the feeling that this book had been co-authored by Mr. Seselj, and Mr. Seselj has just indicated that this book, that he did not author this book and that somebody wrote a book about him and about what he -- about what he had said, which is not quite the same thing. What do you have to say to this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, we would have to see the book, but I agree that it was co-authored, and my understanding is also that Mr. Seselj is the editor of the book. I will check that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Seselj, the witness is telling us that you are a co-author to this book and that you had the book published. From what I understood, you are neither the publisher nor the author of this book.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I handed this book over to the Prosecutor in the courtroom together with a set of 80 of my books in 2003. That's when I handed this book over to the Prosecutor, and the Prosecutor has had ample time to study the book carefully. Now, I can provide it to the Trial Chamber to have a look at and you can see that the majority of the book is written by Sinisa Aksentijevic, that he is the author of the majority. Now, my quotations are under quotation marks, and you can see that in certain fragments which have been translated. Now, in English there are inverted commas where my quotations are used. I can provide you with the original to see this for yourselves. So on the book it says Dr. Vojislav Seselj in the camera lens of Sinisa Aksentijevic. So it's how Sinisa Aksentijevic sees me and it's a set of three books. The three book -- the first book was entitled well it was number 51 it says Vojislav Seselj in the claws of the book of Mirjana Bobic-Mojsilovic. She's a famous Serb journalist and she conducted interviews with me and published a book. The second book in the series is Vojislav Seselj under the lens magnifying glass of Kostic, and she is a journalist in the sphere of economics, and it is devoted to economic issues. Now the third book in this series was by the editor-in-chief of the paper Serbia, Sinisa Aksentijevic and it is a collage of his own texts, my quotations, and sporadic interviews and talks with me and he published a number of documents too. I can hand the book over. I have another copy in the detention centre and you can have a look at it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll take a look at this. Please take a -- get the book and the Trial Chamber will take a look at it. Witness, you heard what Mr. Seselj just said. It seems that three books were written about him by different people regarding different topics, but it's not because a book is written about you, but you're necessarily the author or the inspiration of this book. So what can you say to this? It is true that when you see the first page there is his picture, and you could -- one could infer from this that he is a co-author, but it seems that everything that's in the book except what's in quotation marks comes from the author of the book.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, if that is what Mr. Seselj states then I'm willing to accept it. I think the most important is to see whether the quotation in my report of this basic agreement, whether that agreement is based on basic military organisations, whether it's authentic or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think the break is coming up. We might have passed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely. It's time for the break. And during the break we will read the book. So we'll have a 20-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The hearing is resumed. During the break the Trial Chamber looked at the document. It is a book written by someone else than Mr. Seselj. Mr. Seselj is asked questions, and he answers these questions. There are also excerpts of speeches. That's it. We cannot drought conclusion from this that Mr. Seselj is the author of this book or the inspiration of this book. This is somebody who wrote a book about Mr. Seselj using Q and As and speeches. The Trial Chamber is now going to hand over the document back to Mr. Seselj. If he wants to present it during the cross-examination he may so, but then we will need a translation into English of the relevant parts, because it is quite a large book. Please resume. Please continue. We have just one hour left.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honour. Before I request the admission of this particular document, I would like to examine a number of other documents with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, the document we just talked about, so that is 1974, on page 3 have an outline of various ranks used by the SRS maybe, or my question is basically this: Based on the material you have reviewed, was this particular structure of ranks ever implemented?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. In particular, the orders from Radical Party to proclaim certain people, certain volunteers to Chetnik Vojvoda, as well as other SRS or SRS War Staff documents, show the use of military ranks, sometimes preceded by the term "Chetnik." So for example they mention Chetnik captain or Chetnik major. JNA documents or VRS documents, however, they will use terms like "Self-styled" or "So-called captain or lieutenant" when they refer to these ranks which had been attributed by the SRS. And there is, for example -- okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: If I may interrupt you?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, what I propose to do now is just run through quickly a number of other exhibits which reflect this -- reflect this particular use of ranks. And if Your Honours would move with me to Exhibit 1446, which is the next document in your binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, is this a document you have referred to in your report?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. I did refer to this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And Your Honours will note that in the first paragraph of the actual text there's reference to platoon commanders, for example, and it's a request that two persons -- three persons be promoted to the rank of lieutenant. Your Honours, if we move on to the next document, which is 65 ter number 770, or --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have an objection. The Prosecutor gave up too quickly on the previous document from the book by Sinisa Aksentijevic, and I know full well why he gave that up so quickly, because I suggested to the president of the registry to have distributed the English translation of a statement made by Captain Radoslav Suljagic, and I submit it for translation two weeks ago in other words ample time and now he sees this document is untenable, why? And now he's going away from it, why? Because in the document, we see that the author relates back to events of 1984, and you can see the document there on page 182, and it says the basic organisation of the volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party. And from the text itself we can see that he refers to experiences gained in 1984, in the third section, and at the top erroneously, the author says that it is a document from June 1991. So that's the main problem. And now the Prosecutor has realised that and is trying to get away from the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I may. I -- it is -- I've not requested the admission of the document yet. I've not looked at the statement the accused is referring to. I am going to request the admission of all of the documents that I'm going to be referring to in this section of the testimony; but I think it's important that we try to gain a certain momentum in the presentation of the evidence if I may and if the accused would be kind enough to make his objections when I seek the admission of the documents rather than comments on everything I do along the way. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, absolutely, Mr. Marcussen. You're right. But Mr. Seselj is talking about documents dealing with events that did not occur in 1984, as we have in the English transcript but in 1994; and it seems if that's the case you're mentioning events that have nothing to do with 1991 or 1992. That's the crux of the problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's my understanding that the book we discussed was published in 1994. The documents about the ranks was published in 1994, and it's a document referring to the basic military structure of the SRS, and the SRS was not in existence in 1994. Sorry, in 1984.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, once again I refer to paragraph 3 of this document where it says that the volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party are continuing a patriotic tradition, and then in the penultimate line it says that the Serbian volunteers and Chetniks in the war from 1991 to 1994. So it's not only the book that was published in 1994. We see that the document was written in 1994, because you can't write a document in 1991 and then say we refer to the traditions from 1991 to 1994. So the Prosecutor must not be allowed to mislead the public or the Trial Chamber. That's what it says in this document if you look at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, my question to the witness was exactly whether or not he -- based on the evidence he has reviewed has seen the implementation of these particular ranks from 19 -- around the time relevant to the indictment. There is no dispute that this document was published in 1994. The question was this document was published in 1994. Have the witness seen any indication that these ranks were implemented before and we're going through a series of documents now which show they were indeed employed and that's the line of examination that we're pursuing and I think that's entirely proper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I think I found the problem. It's not very easy to understand it. The objection and the answer were not that easy to understand. This document 796 which comes from the book that we've seen earlier does mention ranks. This is on page 3 and 4. Well, it seems that we have mention of the ranks of the volunteers. Now, the question is whether this document that we have on page 3 was drafted in 1991 or in 1994, because then of course this is essential. If it was drafted in 1990, 1991, then we understand why the Prosecutor is showing us documents on this ranking, such as document 1446. Witness, please, the document from the Serbian Radical Party which establishes ranks, could you tell us what year it dates from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... from the book, Your Honour, is that this document, the basic military organisation, is published in 1994. However, what I've tried to show in the report is that certain aspects of that document were already implemented in 1991. I have information often ranks. I also have information on the use of military names of structures in order to identify the SRS volunteer formations as well as also, thirdly, the use of military terminology to explain the role or to describe the role of volunteers. And these documents, for example, say, well, Mr. X was in command of the SRS volunteer detachment in that and that area, or he was a deputy commander, and related examples.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So if I understand what you've just said, for you 1991 and 1992 is the period when this text on ranks was already applied. Is that it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... we apply something that is issued or that becomes public in 1994. What I tried to say is that the information that is included in a document of 1994 is actually already applicable in 1991, 1992, because ranks are being used. Names of military structures are being used, and also military terminology is being used. And whether it was published in 1994 or 1993 does not change what was happening in 1991 or 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So if I go along with what you're saying, let's look at document 1446 where one person is proposed to be promoted to the rank of lieutenant. Three persons are proposed to be promoted to the rank of lieutenant. Let's imagine that the War Staff of the Serbian Radical Party allows this, allows for this. I have the following question thus: These three people who were maybe -- who maybe belong to TOs, TO units or JNA units, how will these units translate their new rank? Otherwise, these are political rank -- this is political ranking a political favour and nothing else and they never become real in the end. But how can you check as -- yourself that this was actually implemented on the -- in the TOs or in the JNA or in the VRS.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would verify that, Your Honour, by looking at JNA or VRS documents that make reference to these people who have been promoted by the SRS. And, for example, we see in at least one VRS document where in connection to an individual Mitar Maksimovic who became known as Manda, and this is in 65 ter 1523, so this is the Tolimir report I believe we will discuss later; Tolimir writes about the self styled captain. So this shows that the ranks are being used also in the field but are not recognised as such by the JNA or the VRS even though the volunteer who has that rank uses it. And when I return then to SRS documents, there I notice that within these SRS volunteer detachments the rank is important to establish the authority the particular volunteer has among the other volunteers. For example, this also applies to the title Vojvoda. From the documents I have reviewed included in the report, it books clear that Chetnik Vojvodas have a position of authority among the other SRS volunteers and use that title even though JNA or VRS do not recognise the title. Another example, for example, that's page 138 in my report, is where mention is made of a Jovan Kulic, who is, according to JNA documents, a self-appointed captain. So I'm not sure whether that answers the question, Your Honour, but that's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. These are self-proclaimed officers or captains. Very well. But they are part of legal units. It's as if yesterday I self-proclaim myself as President of this Tribunal. This would have no effect. I mean, my colleagues wouldn't really care about it because there is already a president of the Tribunal. Or if Mr. Marcussen self-proclaimed himself Prosecutor in chief. I mean this would have no effect after all. So there is a difference between self-proclaiming oneself and holding a rank in the army. There is a distinction, what do you think of this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To follow on the example you made about yourself, the problem starts when there are people who will follow you, when or Mr. Marcussen says, I am now the Prosecutor. Well, if there are people in the OTP who will start following Mr. Marcussen and recognise this kind of self-proclamation, then the problem starts, because then Mr. Marcussen will have a position of authority over these people. And that is actually the conclusion I draw from, on the one hand, the use of these ranks in the SRS and they call it a Chetnik captain or SRS captain and on the other hand the positions these people hold on the ground even though it's not recognised by the JNA still within the volunteer detachment, these people have authority.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but the unit that is going on the field, did it follow the orders of JNA commander or did it follow the orders of those self-proclaimed commanders that had been proclaimed by the Serbian Radical Party?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can explain to you an example of Vukovar where we have seen the structure of Operational Group south and then we had had a number of assault detachments subordinated to Operational Group south and then we had a number of assault detachments subordinated to Operation Group south and these assault detachments consisted of assault groups; were on the lowest level you would have in one sole group you would have JNA soldiers of the Guards Brigade, members of the TO Serbia, as well as the Leva Supoderica detachment and the commander of that Leva Supoderica detachment, so a SRS detachment, Milan Lancuzanin also known as Kameni, was the person who was recognised by the JNA officer in command of the assault group as being the person in command of the volunteers. So the volunteers unit is then actually a separate component of the assault group. You could consider it as a separate company in a battalion, whereas a traditional battalion consists of three companies, well there would be a fourth company, a volunteer company, and the commander of that company, of that volunteer detachment was someone with in a position of hierarchy among the SRS volunteers who had been appointed a position by the members of the Serbian Radical Party War Staff. Sometimes that position was confirmed by the JNA, sometimes not. So it depends of the area, and even though there is single command and control, the way how this is being implemented in the field differs from area to area, i.e., that is that people with -- who have received authority from the Serbian Radical Party war -- Serbian Radical Party War Staff use that authority among their volunteers.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection. Mr. President; I'm intervening because the witness is trying to mislead you by quoting a concrete example. He said that Colonel Tolimir called Mitar Maksimovic self-appointed captain. Mitar Maksimovic, Manda. He was not a volunteer of the Serbian Radical Party. He was a local of Ugljevik in Republika Srpska in Bosnia-Herzegovina. Yes, he was a member of the Serbian Radical Party but he wasn't a volunteer which the party from Serbia sent to the front, but as local inhabitant of his village he rose up to fight. So that's a basic difference. And I don't think the witness should use this kind of thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: This is a good example of cross-examination -- a cross-examination point, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, now if we follow on in the -- in the binder, 65 ter number 770, which is also P25, Mr. Theunens, is this another document which you have referred to on this particular point? I know many of these documents you referred to in many different parts of your report, but on the issue of use of ranks, what does this document tell us?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document is a request to promote a number of people who were identified as warriors, so it shows, first of all, structure for example Petrova Gora TO detachment the use of military terminology to express the authority like it talks about Chetnik commander and then obviously it also shows also rank.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And if we go to the next document which is 7601 [sic], what we have here is a certificate from the War Staff to Branislav Gavrilovic. And Your Honours will see that this document again certifies that he was a commander of a group of volunteers. And 761, if you turn the page, is a similar document with respect to Miroslav Vukovic. Oh, in line -- on page 89, line 20, I think there's a problem misspoke there. The 65 ter number reference should be 761. Your Honours, the witness has referred to the promotion of a number of people to Vojvoda and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe we could have this last document on the screen, because it's interesting, because it was actually signed by Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honour. The two last ones I've shown, I believe -- no, sorry. Sorry. Excuse me. Only 761.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, had you looked into this document in the preparation of your report?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, I did, and it's included in my report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What conclusions do you draw from the examination of this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I will be very brief. It shows the use of military terminology in the sense that a person is given authority here by Mr. Seselj, and his title is deputy commander of volunteers. It also shows that these volunteers are operating in a separate unit. And to return to what we discussed earlier today, it also shows that the Serb Radical Party or the War Staff are keeping records of what volunteers are doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And -- and maybe if we -- to go a little more --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection. Mr. President, I think that you should caution the witness and tell him that he can't mislead you in this fashion. On the -- on the document, it says certificate that somebody was a commander whereas the witness is saying that I issued authorisation on the basis of this piece of paper. I just assert that he was a commander of the volunteers during that period of time. So it's just a certificate. I'm not giving authorisation. So he's misleading you there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm looking at this certificate, Witness. If you review it very carefully without drawing any conclusions one way or the other, if you try to remain very objective when assessing this document, you find that someone called Vukovic was the deputy commander of volunteers on the territory of the Serbian district of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem from the 4th of June to the 2nd of December, 1991. This document is signed by two persons. We have a certificate stating that this person named Vukovic was the deputy commander of volunteers. That's what we can see when reading this document. But you draw further conclusions from the review of this document, don't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, because it is signed by the president of a political either as well as -- okay, in this particular case as chief of the War Staff. So at least the document shows that -- that Mr. Seselj and the chief of the War Staff have the authority to issue such certificates. Now, these are not the kind of diplomas I think you get for attending a course somewhere or a certificate of achievement, because from documents that I have reviewed where the payment of volunteers is being discussed, the time period spent on the battlefield is essential in order to determine which allowances the volunteers are entitled to. So this document would then show that the SRS -- SRS War Staff have the authority to issue such certificates to certain volunteers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me take another example. Let me take the Belgian example. Let's assume that we have a Belgian soldier who is a member of environment association, and he asks the president of this association to deliver him a certificate stating that he is a member of the association, and then the president of this association would probably write a certificate stating, "I certify that such-and-such person who is a captain," and so on and so forth, "served in this -- this country from that date to that date." What would you say then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would first try to find out what the service was about. If he's serving somewhere was a volunteer, as a deputy commander of volunteers, that would indicate to me that he's accomplishing military tasks, and it would be rather -- second point would then be it would be rather unusual for the president of an environmental association or the president of political party to issue such certificates, because we are dealing with military matters, and the use of military force is indicated by law and not by individual political parties or movements.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, if you would again go to the next tab in your binder we have 65 ter number 1841, and this document can be broadcast to the public.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, I believe this is one of the documents you referred to in your report on the issue of appointments of Vojvodas; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And as we just talked about Mr. Vukovic, if Your Honours go to page 2 of the document you will see Mr. Vukovic mentioned here and his time -- the places here served are being mentioned in this particular document. You will also, if you turn to the next page, under item 6 see Mr. Gavrilovic being mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, if you turn to the next document, 2030.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment, please. You're going too fast. Let's have a look at document 1841, dated 13th of May, 1993, and signed apparently by Mr. Seselj. By this document a number of Vojvodas are proclaimed. Several individuals are going to be promoted to the title of Vojvoda. I'm trying to count how many there are. Ah, 16. Sixteen people are going to be proclaimed Vojvoda, including this Vukovic person we mentioned earlier on, and we can find him at number 5. Please -- okay. This is a proclamation by which these people are named Vojvoda. Do you see the introduction to this document? Can you see it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What conclusion do you draw from reading this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That Mr. Seselj considers himself in the position to reward certain volunteers for their role in the conflict, which he defines the role, and I'm reading it: "Exceptional merits in this war, great courage and demonstrated war skills of the most prominent Chetnik commanders."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They are proclaimed Vojvodas. What are the implications of such a proclamation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, these implications are similar as what we discussed with the use of ranks or Chetnik ranks or SRS ranks by the war staff. That is that the volunteers, the SRS volunteers who are proclaimed Vojvoda are confirmed in a position of authority within the SRS War Staff and the SRS volunteer detachments and also use this title during operations even though this title is not respected which the JNA or -- the JNA did not exist any more in 1993, but by the VRS or the SVK in Croatia. But still like as we see in Sarajevo, when the VRS commander complains about the behaviour of certain SRS volunteers, they will use the term Vojvoda but within quotation marks to show that they don't recognise it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Amongst these 16 individuals who were proclaimed Vojvoda, did you try to find out what consequence this had on their personal situation, on their personal status within the armed forces? Did it bring them anything or was this a purely honourary title for them that they could brag with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For example, Your Honours, looking at the first one, Slavo Aleksic, well he, when we studied -- looked at the situation in Sarajevo, Aleksic is the commander of a unit known as the Novo Sarajevo Chetnik detachment. He's in Novo Sarajevo so Grabovica in command of a number of volunteers and this is based on the VRS Sarajevo-Romanija Corps documents I reviewed. He is recognised in that position. He is considered the commander. He's not being removed. He is the person they talk to when they have tasks or operations to conduct within the Novo Sarajevo Chetnik detachment. The same applies to other volunteers. Milan Lancuzanin, we have to go back in time then, but he was the commander of the Leva Supoderica TO detachment and was respected as such by the members of the Guards Motorised Brigade in Vukovar. Srecko Radovanovic plays a leading role in the local Serb TO in Western Slavonia. Okay. Sometimes this refers to events prior to the proclamation to Vojvoda, but the proclamation to Vojvoda confirms the position of authority, and the people who received the title use it in their -- while carrying out their duties in charge of SRS volunteers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but very quickly let's go back to number 1, to the number 1, to Aleksic, who is a commander in Sarajevo. He was appointed commander, but who appointed him? Was he appointed to this position by the army, or was he appointed by Mr. Seselj? Because this sentence here doesn't mean anything. He was appointed and so on and so forth. He may have gone up through the ranks, as is customary, without the SRS having to interfere, to help his promotion. If we look at Kameni, it's the same if you read what's written here about him. Did his promotion through the ranks -- does he have to -- or is it because of the SRS or is it because of what he did at the head of this unit? That's the problem we have. We, the Judges, find it difficult to establish the link, because -- between the title of Vojvoda that is given to someone and the practical implications of such title in the field.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, to -- to start with Slavko Aleksic, based on the documents I have reviewed, Aleksic had no military rank nor military experience or significant military experience, which means that he was appointed to the position he held by the SRS or an organ of the SRS. And even if he was not appointed, because there are examples where individuals say, "I am now the commander of this detachment," he is recognised and confirmed in that position by the SRS War Staff or the SRS. In the section on Sarajevo in part 2 of the report, I've included a few documents which indicate that Aleksic is on the pay list of the local police, local Serb police, as a reserve policeman. Now, Lancuzanin, Lancuzanin was already a person with a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me interrupt you once again, because you are giving us an additional detail that's only confusing matters. If this Aleksic was paid by the Serbian local police, that would mean that the SRS controlled the police and the operation of the police forces.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't think we can draw that conclusion, Your Honours, and I apologise if I contribute to confusion, but I just want to highlight how complicated the situation is. It is not as straightforward as it would be in the French, Italian or Danish army or in Belgium where you're a member of the armed forces, full stop, and there are procedures for promotion. There are procedures for discipline. There are procedures for anything. Here we see that obviously in the SFRY things were clearly regulated by law, SFRY armed forces with JNA, TO, we had police forces but then in the conflict structures split according to ethnic lines. We have a local Serb TO in Croatia. The Croatians organise their own forces. The same that happens to the police. The same happens in Bosnia-Herzegovina. And in that situation, we also see that political parties are establishing -- or at least organising groups which could be considered armed groups. Sometimes it's just to recruitment of volunteers but at other times it's really creating paramilitary forces. And these forces are acting in the field, most often under the command of the JNA as far as Croatia is concerned, and then Bosnia-Herzegovina JNA and -- or VRS, but there are sometimes different situations. And this is what I've tried to highlight in the report. Now, what I can say in relation to the SRS Vojvodas or Chetnik Vojvodas is these are all people with a position of authority among the volunteers. They are commanders on the field of these volunteers and are respected as such both by the volunteers as well as the armed forces, JNA or VRS they are operating with even though there are situation where is it seems that the volunteer detachment has its own agenda, that's why there are so many documents included in the report. Or senior members of the SRS War Staff are promoted to Chetnik Vojvoda. Whether it changes something in relation to their position of authority they already had is difficult to ascertain but at least among the SRS volunteers a Vojvoda has significant authority and even charisma.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection. Mr. President, this time maybe my objection is not appropriate. You will be the judge of that and if you say it is not appropriate I'll withdraw it, but I think great confusion is being created here because the witness obviously and sufficiently well knows certain things, so it would be best if he could clarify first of all which one out of these 16 Chetnik Vojvodas was a volunteer of the Serbian Radical Party that was sent by the party to the front line and who is a local resident of the place where military operations were taking place and subsequently joined the Serbian Radical Party and then subsequently was proclaimed by me a Chetnik Vojvoda because of his merits during the war. This distinction has to be made first lest we create an even greater confusion if you think my objection is inappropriate, I will withdraw.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your objection is quite valid. You could raise it during cross-examination, but what I'm concerned about is to address the heart of the matter. Now, among those 16 people it's very difficult to tell which ones were initially members of the SRS and which ones as part of action undertaken by the SRS were sent off as volunteers to fulfil military obligations. So we may be confronted with a situation -- with a situation where local people during the conflict become members of the party without the SRS having initiated in a form of conversion and something that may have changed their military position, and afterwards they're rewarded by being given the title Vojvoda. So as you can understand, you are an expert witness. The situation sometimes can be very complex. Do you stand by what you've said, or do you wish to change your conclusion somewhat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, it is indeed correct that there are locals among the volunteers, so people who lived in the area where they then established a volunteer group with or without the support of the Serbian Radical Party. As well as people who were sent from other areas to the particular conflict zones. For example, I mean --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Again the example of Kameni, for instance. He comes from Vukovar. So he wasn't sent by -- because he was already on the spot.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Lancuzanin I have included in the report documents from the SRS War Staff or at least one document indicating that he is the commander of the Leva Supoderica detachment, and I'm just trying to locate the document. Or at least that links the Leva Supoderica detachment to the -- to the SRS. It's a Velika Srbija article. Now, when we look for example at Branislav Vakic, he's number 3 on the -- on the Vojvoda proclamation order on number 24. It's on the second page. Branislav Vakic was born in Nis. Nis is a city in southern Serbia. And there you see the CV according to the SRS. Now, the information I reviewed in preparation for the report and as for example an article on war days of Branislav Vakic shows that he's being sent by the SRS or the SRS War Staff to the various combat zones; it's not that individual decides that tomorrow I go and fight in Vukovar because he needs -- he doesn't go on his own. He needs military equipment. He needs to have a uniform. He needs to be authorised to enter the war zone. Once he's there he needs to be supported logistically with food, ammunition, if necessary fuel, and so and so on; so it's not individuals who decide about I'm going to defend or I'm going to fight for a certain cause now this is part of a bigger set-up. Therefore, the SRS War Staff. And there are other people were from the location where they were born. If we go, for example, to number 5, Miroslav Vukovic. He's born in Cacak. Cacak is located in -- in Northern Serbia. Branislav Gavrilovic is indeed born in Sarajevo but we know that he's also active if Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem, and also in Brcko. So other areas than just the location where he was to defend his own area where he was born.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, as -- as you have surely noticed, the last part of the second part of the report has quite a detailed overview of all the relevant crime bases and pattern bases where these matters are discussed by the expert in great detail. I hope we'll be able to cover that part during the testimony as well, but there's extensive information on these issues in that part of the report. With leave of the Court, I would maybe move on to the -- the next exhibit, which is 2030, which is another document referred to by Mr. Theunens in his report. It's -- it's another of these Vojvoda appointment documents. As we have dealt with the other one in detail, maybe we don't need to -- I wasn't intending to go so much into this one but rather to ask the witness about the following document, which is 2038, which also relates to the issue of Vojvodas.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: But Mr. Theunens, could you tell us what this document is and what it shows. It is order number 156.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is an order by Mr. Seselj whereby he strips three individuals of the title of Vojvoda. These individuals are mentioned in the document as well as the reasons why Mr. Seselj took the decision to remove the title of Vojvoda of these people.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, in the interest of time I was not going to cover the issue of ranks any more but move on to the issue of reports received by the War Staff. If there's no questions from the Bench to the witness about the use of ranks, I would like to request the admission of the exhibits that we have been discussing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Registrar, could we have exhibit numbers, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I can just read out what the 6 at that ter numbers were they were 1974.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, P213.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It's P214.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Which has to be places under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And then 770, which is P25 which has been marked for identification, but I'd like to request the admission full admission of the document at this stage and under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. That will be Exhibit number P25 under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Then 65 ter number 760, again under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Exhibit number 215.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P215.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I'm just reading out a number of exhibit numbers if I can complete that maybe you would be kind enough to raise the other issue afterwards; then we have had 65 ter number 1841 which can be public.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours that will be Exhibit P217.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: We've had 2030 which can be public.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, that will be Exhibit P218.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And then 2038 which.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours Exhibit P219.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And I believe the accused had an objection on the mark.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, what did you want to say?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I strenuously oppose that any of these documents be under seal. I insist that you accept the solution that you had accepted a moment ago, not to mention the source of the document but to speak publicly and openly about the contents because the documents are public by their very nature. I'm not interested in how the Prosecution got the documents but the contents is important to me, and they are important to the public. They are originally public. None of them bears the mark confidential. The Serbian Radical Party has some confidential documents but these are not that type. We even have rules and how to treat confidential documents. These ones are open. Don't make them secret.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues] ... that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe we have just been in public session discussing these documents and that was exactly your -- your request. Now, if it facilitate matters, what I can propose is we, the Prosecution, can redact the parts of these documents once we have reviewed what is being said on the transcript of this, and we can place them without the part that identifies the source. So at a later stage we can essentially have a public version of these documents put on record if that facilitate in avoiding these kind of issues coming up all the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, indeed. Your idea is quite attractive but may come up against the following difficulty: As these documents are already well-known documents, they've been published somewhere, let us assume that someone wishes to compare these public documents with the redacted documents and the person then realises that some of the names have been redacted, the person will understand straight away.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honour. I think the main concern would be to redact the part that I showed you in private session, which is a very clear indication of what the source is. I'm just floating this for Your Honour's consideration to facilitate matters. We don't need to decide on it now maybe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Bench will reflect on it and will not take a decision right now, but I would like to get back to the document 2030 and order number 156, where seemingly four people have had their title of Vojvoda taken away from them. I have read the reasons which have been put forward why these people have lost their title, and the last reason is something which attracted my attention. One of them or several of them would have been recruited by the services of the MUP. It seems that a Vojvoda who has been recruited by or who is working for the Ministry of the Interior is sufficient reason to mistrust the person in question. What do you have to say about this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, this -- this applies in particular to number 3 on the list, whereby, and this is public knowledge at the time, whereby Mr. Seselj suspected that person of having, yeah, particular links, i.e., that he was collecting information for the state security of the Republic of Serbia. And I remember that there was at a time when this person was kicked out of the War Staff a press conference whereby this person more or less had to make a confession about his ties with the Serbian Radical Party -- excuse me, with the state security of the Republic of Serbia, with Mr. Seselj sitting on his left or his right side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This event indicates that in the Republic of Serbia there were power struggles or between the political parties, the MUP, and the Ministry of the Interior. There was a struggle to exert influence; is that right? Can you confirm this.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... and more specifically that the competent services, i.e., the State Security Service was aware that certain political parties were organising, I mean, recruiting, organising, dispatching volunteers and also involved in arming them, and that from the legal point of view it made sense to keep an eye on that even though it seems that it took some time before there was any action against these activities. This is not dealt with in my report, but I remember that it's only after a political conflict arises between Mr. Seselj and Mr. Milosevic sometimes in October, November 1993 that the competent authorities in Serbia start with the arrest of volunteers, and they're all arrested -- or most of them are arrested on the ground of illegal possession of firearms, and they're released quite soon. So whether it's part of a bigger struggle I haven't looked into these -- these aspects, but I can -- I can confirm what I just said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now we have four minutes left, Mr. Marcussen. You have the floor.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Mr. President, if you allow me. You as the Trial Chamber instructed the Prosecution a while ago to make available to me documents they got from the government of the Republic of Serbia for which certain protective measures were requested. It's a large number of documents attesting that the security service kept me and my advisors under surveillance and persecuted us in a way in the time relevant for the indictment. These documents would be important to me in tomorrow's cross-examination of this witness, because they refute the theory of joint criminal enterprise involving me and Slobodan Milosevic and some others. On one hand, it is obvious that we were persecuted by the police, and the -- on the other hand, we were supposed to be in league with them. We got some documents from the Prosecution so far, but there is a whole set we haven't received.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. To -- to address that issue first. As Your Honour know, there is a request for protective measures of these documents that is pending before the Trial Chamber. The Prosecution has taken steps to allow us to disclose all of these documents under Rule 66(B) to the accused. What has been done is a letter has been sent to the relevant authorities, and we're waiting for an answer from the authorities on the issues of protective measures. As soon as we have clarified that, we hope to be in a position to provide the documents to the accused. The documents were provided to us with restrictions, and we're not at this stage in a position to give them to the accused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I've understood you correctly, the Republic of Serbia sent you some documents. You are asking the Republic of Serbia the permission to disclose these documents to the accused. Is that right? Is that what you're telling us? And that if the -- if Serbia says yes, you will disclose the documents. If Serbia says no, then you are bound by the rules of Rule 70, i.e., when one of the party discloses documents to -- discloses documents it has the monopoly of these documents; is that right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Yes. The documents were provided with a certain number of clauses as to what cases the documents could be used in and requesting the Prosecution to notify the Republic of Serbia of the Prosecution's intended use, so we have notified the Republic of Serbia of our intention to disclose these documents. Because of the protective measures that have been requested, we think it's appropriate to give the Republic of Serbia a certain amount of time, a limited amount of time to respond to us if there are any concerns about disclosure of any of these documents. As soon as we have that response, we're prepared to disclose the documents to the accused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Seselj, you have understood that for the time being, unfortunately, as far as you're concerned, the Prosecutor cannot disclose those documents because the Prosecutor is bound to its commitment to the Republic of Serbia. So the Prosecution is awaiting the response of the Republic of Serbia. So even if you feel that this may stand in the way of your cross-examination, that's the way things stand. If the Republic of Serbia had disclosed nothing whatsoever, then of course this would not even be mentioned today.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the Prosecution gave me a list of those documents. According to my information, my knowledge, the Republic of Serbia provided those documents unconditionally, and then subsequently minister Rasim Lajic got the idea that he should request protective measures from these documents. Originally they were given to the Prosecution unconditionally. Yesterday again I addressed to you a written submission requesting that you should make these documents completely public and to enable me to use these documents in the cross-examination of this witness and the following ones. I think it concerns 800 or 900 documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Marcussen, from what I understood, when Serbia had sent you the list of documents the Republic of Serbia had clearly indicated that some of these documents were sensitive documents, because this -- these could have repercussions on the people mentioned in the documents themselves. I believe that that is what was said in the message. And you are telling us that you put the question to the Republic of Serbia again and you asked them which documents could be disclosed to Mr. Seselj. Is that right? Is that how things happened?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I think we have taken a slightly more assertive line. We have informed the Republic of Serbia of our intention to disclose these documents and requested the Republic of Serbia to revert to us in case there are any concerns, and we're waiting for this response and I'll be happy to check today on the status of -- of this, because as I -- we already indicated I think we have already indicated that we would [overlapping speakers] disclose these documents. And on the issue of cross-examination, maybe the -- that is if once the accused receive the documents and could show good cause for this the witness can be called back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In any case, you have all afternoon to phone Belgrade and tell them that you need a response urgently because Mr. Seselj might find it useful to have those documents in his possession. This could be settled very quickly. Maybe there are other concerns, but there is a trial ongoing and this does require all and everyone's attention. So we now have to adjourn. I would prefer to continue, but unfortunately I can't. There are other people perhaps who may wish to use this courtroom. We shall meet again tomorrow at 12.00. The hearing will last an hour and a half. Then we shall have a break at 1.30, and an hour's break to enable Mr. Seselj to have something to eat, the interpreters, and maybe the Prosecutor as well, as then we will resume at a quarter past 2.00. So see you tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 20th day of February, 2008, at 12.00 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.47 p.m.,
